messages:
dan: noticed a prod OOM spike on an inf-heavy customer at 09:12 UTC, looks correlated with long-context sessions >120k tokens
priya: saw it too, alerted by kv.slab_alloc_rate and high frag ratio, happening after yesterday's kernel selector flip to auto_kernel_v2
jess: timeline? did the rollout coincide with the spike window?
dan: yes, kernel flip to auto_kernel_v2 at 08:45, first OOM at 09:09, multiple retries then hard OOM at 09:12
theo: grabbing profiles now — running perf on a repro load. rough summary: per-token transient allocations increased and we see a "staircase" of slab growth with sparse reuse (holes)
priya: attaching small snippet of the heaptrace we captured:
```
slab 0x7f..: 8MB -> 24MB -> 56MB (repeated allocations, 64B alignment gaps)
kv_page_count: 820 -> 1340 -> 2100 (paging kicked in)
frag_ratio: 0.48 -> 0.67
```
jess: that frag ratio jump explains why paging couldn't reclaim fast enough — background evict hooks were starved by the kernel path taking long-lived temp allocations
dan: immediate mitigation I rolled: reverted kernel selector back to auto_kernel_v1 for that ASG, enabled kv.autoevict_force=true and lowered max_kv_pages to 1024 for the fleet at 09:21
deploy-bot: revert to auto_kernel_v1 started (deploy id dpl-4321) :arrow_heading_down:
infra-bot: auto-evict ON for cluster r-inference-prod-3, max_kv_pages=1024
priya: post-mitigation telemetry: slab_alloc_rate dropped 70%, frag_ratio down to ~0.35, no further OOMs in the 30m window
theo: root cause hypothesis: auto_kernel_v2 changed allocation churn (temporary buffers not returned to slab quickly) which caused allocation pattern mismatch with our KV slab coalescer and LRU evict heuristics
jess: short-term action items: 1) keep kernel selector on v1 for production until we have a guarded rollout 2) add per-request fallback: if kv.slab_frag_ratio>0.6 then force non-kv path for that request 3) alert on kv.slab_growth_rate and kv.longctx_count
dan: longer term: patch kernel allocator to reduce short-lived heap paths or make slab coalescer aware of the new allocator's free patterns; also implement incremental compaction + emergency drain that doesn't block token streaming
priya: will write a one-pager and owner for compaction work (cc @theo). I'll open a tracking RFC and a perf test that simulates longctx token growth patterns
theo: I have a repro harness that reproduces staircase within 5k requests, will add to CI perf suite and run kernel A/B in canary with traffic shaping
jess: also adding a graceful-degrade playbook: - soft-fallback to smaller model variant if kv unavailable - per-request retry with exponential backoff and a single fuzzy-cache attempt - metricized knob kv.force_non_kv=true for emergency toggles
dan: thanks all — next steps: priya write RFC by EOD, theo add perf job, jess draft playbook. we'll sync in Ops huddle at 10:30 to decide permanent rollback or guarded rollout timeline :thumbsup:
priya: logging action items in #incidents and will tag SRE for runbook updates
dan: closing thread for now, will append postmortem once we have root cause and patch merged
